items.item_text: Experience in aseptic technique and circulation in an OR.
Experience in a clinical hospital setting with various species performing sedation and anesthesia.

Independent of supervision in a hospital setting, as a significant part of daily duties, responsible for treatment of patients with life-threatening illness or injury, whose conditions are likely to change on a moment-to-moment basis and inducing and monitoring anesthesia. Under the direction of the Small Animal Neurology Supervisor and the Neurology/Neurosurgery Service Chief, provide technical support to the Neurology/Neurosurgery service. Responsibilities include but are not limited to anesthesia induction, anesthesia monitoring, surgical preparation for various procedures, circulation in the operating room, training of various technical skills to students or residents, patient treatments, diagnostic sample collection and performing technical skills such as IV catheter placement, blood draws, urinary catheter placement. Additional responsibilities include client communication and education, patient admission and discharge, and working cooperatively with others to foster strong team commitments towards achieving Neurology service objectives.
Ability to recognize peri-anesthetic problems and patient concerns and to effectively communicate problems or concerns to the supervising veterinarian in a timely manner.
Knowledge of normal laboratory values for cats and dogs.
